clue.text: No 6 in this paper's fiscal reports etc.

indicators.note: 'No' plus a number means that entry's answer is left out of the paper's name

parts.note: the puzzle appears in the Financial Times
the answer to 6 across in this grid

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to the newspaper's own pages of fiscal reports and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the newspaper's title and remove the word that answers 6 across; what remains is a word for company accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Financials is a business noun for a company's published accounts and results.

clue.text: Jeer at loud bumpkin

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a lout is a clumsy, uncouth fellow

explanation.surface: Mocking a noisy country yokel.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout once meant to mock or scoff, a sense close to jeering at someone.

clue.text: They want extremely nice ducks to leave India

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: first and last letters of nice

indicators.note: something told to leave departs, so that letter drops out of the birds

parts.note: India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone wants some really nice ducks to be removed from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Needers are people in need, so they want or lack something.

clue.text: Never upset lonely non-U Tory

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An isolated, socially unacceptable Conservative is never upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class. The answer is a jokey British phrase for 'certainly not', from rhyming slang (Nelly Duff, puff, breath of life).
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom is an emphatic refusal, meaning 'no way' or 'never'.

clue.text: Unfit sort who could tie up mischievous kid?

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child
a roper is someone who ties things with rope

explanation.surface: An unsuitable type who might tie up a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: The roper is shown tying up the imp: the wordplay puts the kid first and the roper after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means unsuitable or inappropriate, so unfit for the purpose or occasion.

clue.text: Fantasy Island's American set located in Los Angeles

indicators.note: something located in a place sits inside it, so these letters go within the city's abbreviation

parts.note: A is a common abbreviation for American
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: An American television fantasy island series being filmed on location in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: Fantasy Island was an American TV series, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Laputa is the imaginary flying island in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Herb reportedly in season

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the herb's name is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A herb said to be in season.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period, as in 'in due season', so it can stand for a stretch of time.

clue.text: Mass start among nudists essentially entering jog

indicators.note: a letter entering a word goes inside it
the essence of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A mass jog among nudists begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like a crowd, but it is the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The introit is the psalm or antiphon sung at the opening of the Catholic Mass.

clue.text: Suitable edge absent from trial surrounding senior copper

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so the shortened trial wraps the officer
what is absent from something is missing, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: Detective Inspector, a senior police rank

explanation.surface: A sharp edge missing from a court trial involving a high-ranking police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means convenient and appropriate for a purpose, so suitable in the circumstances.

clue.text: British, outwardly watchful, note retreat around Kensington monument

indicators.note: being outward means being on the outside, so the watchful word wraps the letter

parts.note: a memo is a short note

indicators.note: turned around, the word is read the other way

explanation.surface: Watchful Britons write a note about a retreat near a Kensington monument.
explanation.walkthrough: The Albert Memorial is the ornate memorial to Prince Albert in Kensington Gardens, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The memorial to Queen Victoria's consort stands in Kensington Gardens, so it is a Kensington monument.

clue.text: Just missing opening record in dance

indicators.note: with its opening missing, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: just and honest both mean fair and upright
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Only missing the opening record at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'only', but it means fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ragtime ballroom dance of the early 1900s.

clue.text: Computer plot confused with map

indicators.note: confused things are jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A computer mixes up a plot of land with a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmtop is a small handheld computer that fits in the palm.

clue.text: Abandoning endeavours here, hotheaded ref not bending

indicators.note: bending things out of shape changes their form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered referee who won't bend the rules makes everyone give up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the point where an effort or relationship can go no further, so attempts are given up there.

clue.text: Overlook Jewish festival

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ignore or leave out, as two words
second meaning: the spring feast commemorating the Exodus

explanation.surface: Forgetting about a Jewish holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over is to skip or disregard; Passover (Pesach) is the Jewish spring festival marking liberation from Egypt.

clue.text: Chief prosecutor's case consisting of commercial irregularities primarily linked to China

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer shell, the first and last letters

parts.note: in can mean made up of, as in 'paid in cash'

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each word

parts.note: initial letters of the two words
rhyming slang: china plate means mate

explanation.surface: A chief prosecutor's case about commercial fraud with Chinese connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is Cockney rhyming slang for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means main or foremost, the same as chief.

clue.text: Thinker perhaps beginning to unravel in nervous condition

indicators.note: one letter placed in a word sits inside it

parts.note: to be in a state is to be agitated

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A thinker starting to come apart in an anxious state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinker' suggests a person; it is Rodin's famous sculpture, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodin's Thinker is a famous bronze sculpture, an example of a statue.

clue.text: Folklore hero heading off terrible stench in underground vault

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the vault word
what heads a word is its first letter, taken off it

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A legendary hero turning away from a dreadful smell in a crypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum is British slang for a stink. Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of English folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Thumb, a boy no bigger than his father's thumb, is a hero of English folklore.

clue.text: Damage cover of inspection panel

indicators.note: a cover wraps the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of inspection
a jury is a panel of jurors

explanation.surface: A damaged cover on an inspection panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panel' reads as a hatch, but it means a group judging a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Injury is harm or damage, done to a body or to a reputation.

clue.text: Shrub I initially prune in one month, right

indicators.note: these letters are set inside the month
initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A gardener first prunes a shrub in a particular month, rightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Juniper is an evergreen coniferous shrub whose berries flavour gin.

clue.text: Field-leading medic enters wooded area

indicators.note: something that enters a place goes inside it

parts.note: a forest is a wooded area

explanation.surface: A top doctor walks into a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field-leading' sounds rural, beside the wood, but it means top of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means first in rank or position, at the head of the field.

clue.text: River one associated with eg Tomsk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the great river of Venezuela
second meaning: one of the Wombles, alongside Tomsk

explanation.surface: A river linked with the Siberian city of Tomsk.
explanation.walkthrough: Tomsk reads as the Russian city, but it is a Womble, one of the burrowing creatures of a British children's TV show, all named after places.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco flows through Venezuela; Orinoco is also the lazy Womble, a companion of Tomsk.

clue.text: Reluctant state Senate evacuated

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: an evacuated building is emptied, so only the outer letters are left

parts.note: first and last letters of Senate

explanation.surface: A reluctant state's Senate chamber has been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun for a political region; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or disinclined, so reluctant to do something.

clue.text: Green stone Victorians dressed

indicators.note: dressed stone is cut and worked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Green stone that the Victorians cut for their buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' reads as a colour of stone; it means environmentally minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green, as a noun, is an environmental campaigner, someone who protects nature.

clue.text: Sizeable group returned joint projection

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine, a fair-sized ensemble

explanation.surface: A large group came back to a joint projection.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry a tenon is the projecting end of timber that fits into a mortise to form a joint.

clue.text: Appealing to the public, East London Borough rings you

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the district goes round the letter

parts.note: Poplar is a district of East London, once a borough

explanation.surface: A popular East London borough telephones you.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is a district by the Docklands in East London, once a borough of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means liked by or suited to ordinary people, so appealing to the public.

clue.text: Conservative and Republican not side-by-side in agreement? One can but imagine such a thing

definitions.text: One can but imagine such a thing

indicators.note: the two letters go inside, but kept apart rather than together

explanation.surface: Conservatives and Republicans agreeing rather than at odds is something you can only dream of.
explanation.walkthrough: The two abbreviations go into the agreement word separately, one each side of its O.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a mythical beast, a creature that exists only in the imagination.

clue.text: Bird runs into body of water scrubbing tail

indicators.note: something put into a word goes inside it
to scrub something is to cancel it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lake is a body of water
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A bird runs into a lake and cleans its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird, such as the skylark.

clue.text: Anarchic urban novel's failing, say

indicators.note: anarchic means lawless and disordered, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A chaotic city novel's shortcoming, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' reads as a flaw in the book; it is a grammatical example, an -ing form used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerund such as 'failing' is a word formed from a verb that functions as a noun, an example of the term.
